purpose: Check whether the PCA truncation that helped the centroid probe (experiment 81: mice1 7.31% versus 5.84% full) also helps the MLP readout, or whether it again only compensates for a weak probe.

data.eeg: public train only, 50 ms log1p counts, per-session z-score on the three training repeats

arms.pca128: PCA fitted per session on the three training repeats, project to 128 components without whitening

readout.model: SpikeClassifier, 2748 classes, hidden 1024, dropout 0, apply_log False
readout.training: AdamW lr 3e-4, weight decay 0, batch 256, clip 5, seed 42, fixed 10 epochs, identical to experiment 77

metrics.ocf: official OCF, fold k=4 only, Hungarian per session block, RNG123 heldout pictures [256:768], reported with the canonical row-z scores used in production

pass_rule.advance: pca128 improves recall32 over base for BOTH mice in at least 3 of 4 folds each AND fold-4 OCF improves for both mice
pass_rule.note: k=128 is fixed here because it was near-optimal for both mice in experiment 81; no other k is tried in this experiment

prohibited: fitting PCA on the held repeat
changing epochs or seed between arms
